title: Reachability under equal register states
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathsf{orc}$ assign a Boolean to each of four query types and each finite bit string, and let $x$ be a finite bit string. For machine states $st$ and $st'$, if $st=st'$ and there is a finite run satisfying the guard from the configuration with control state $l$, register vector encoded by $st'$, memory $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, and head position $p\in\mathbb Z$ to a configuration $c$, then there is such a run from the configuration with the same control state, memory, and head position and register vector encoded by $st$, to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: Oracle with four query types and finite bit-string inputs
A guarded finite run exists from the configuration encoded by $st'$ to $c$
replaced:
Fix the machine, oracle, input, register bound, and memory bound. For states $S,S'$ of
the machine's register system, if $S=S'$, then every guarded finite run from the
configuration with control state $\ell$, register values encoded by $S'$, memory
contents $M$, and memory head at $p$ to a configuration $c$ is also such a run from the
configuration with the same control state, memory, and head position but register values
encoded by $S$.
